papers.title: DeepMimic: Example-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning of Physics-Based Character Skills
papers.authors_short: Peng, Abbeel, Levine, van de Panne
papers.code_status: public, MIT, last push 2025-11-27 (GitHub API, 2026-09-23); maintained successor xbpeng/MimicKit (Apache-2.0) implements DeepMimic, AMP, ASE, ADD
papers.api_title: DeepMimic: Example-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning of Physics-Based Character Skills
papers.core_idea: Tracks one reference clip with weighted exponential-kernel rewards: pose exp(-2Σ‖Δq‖²), velocity exp(-0.1Σ‖Δq̇‖²), end-effector exp(-40Σ‖Δp‖²), centre of mass exp(-10‖Δp_c‖²), weights 0.65/0.1/0.15/0.1. A phase variable in the state, reference state initialization and early termination are critical.
papers.what_to_take: SMAT's unspecified phase handling maps onto DeepMimic's phase variable, RSI and early termination. Its pose and velocity kernels differ 20-fold (2 vs 0.1), unlike SMAT's shared exp(-8·err²); pin SMAT's error units before tuning.
papers.left_untested: Torque-driven PD characters only: no muscles, no gait metrics such as symmetry or toe-off. The authors list the need for a synchronized phase variable as a limitation.
papers.feasibility_notes: Trivial to reimplement in MyoAssist; maintained reference code in MimicKit (Apache-2.0).

papers.title: KINESIS: Motion Imitation for Human Musculoskeletal Locomotion
papers.code_status: public, BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE.md), last push 2026-02-03 (GitHub API, 2026-09-23); AMASS motions obtained separately
papers.api_title: KINESIS: Motion Imitation for Human Musculoskeletal Locomotion
papers.core_idea: Model-free PPO imitation for MyoSuite leg models (80 to 290 muscles) on 1.8 h of KIT locomotion from AMASS. Reward: keypoint exp(-200Σ‖Δp‖²), velocity exp(-5Σ‖Δv‖²), L1+L2 activation energy, optional upright term; reference-state starts, 0.15 m termination, hard-negative mining, mixture of experts.
papers.what_to_take: Closest open MuJoCo muscle-imitation recipe: weights w_pos 0.6, w_vel 0.2; 150 Hz simulation, 30 Hz control; direct muscle control beat PD control. Activations correlated with EMG better than alternatives on the same model.
papers.left_untested: No target-speed walking, symmetry or toe-off metrics, and no exoskeleton. KIT clips average about 6 s (1054 clips, 1.8 h), so no steady 1.25 m/s reference is isolated.
papers.feasibility_notes: Trained on one A100 plus 128 CPU threads; MuscleMimic cites ~10 days for the 290-muscle model. BSD-3-Clause code.

papers.title: Musculoskeletal Motion Imitation for Learning Personalized Exoskeleton Control Policy in Impaired Gait
papers.code_status: no code link in arXiv v1 HTML (checked 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: Musculoskeletal Motion Imitation for Learning Personalized Exoskeleton Control Policy in Impaired Gait
papers.core_idea: A 90-muscle Hyfydy model imitates one Scherpereel subject's treadmill clip (0.6 to 2.2 m/s, mirrored for symmetry) with SAC. The DeepMimic-style reward adds joint-torque tracking, metabolic-energy and excitation-smoothness terms; fine-tuning adds hip or ankle exoskeleton torque and simulated muscle weakness.
papers.what_to_take: Published gains (position −2, velocity −0.05, root −500, end-effector −80, torque −2) and sagittal mirroring of the reference to enforce bilateral symmetry, a direct lever for SMAT's r>0.92 target.
papers.left_untested: Simulation only; one-subject reference; no ablation of mirroring or torque tracking on symmetry or toe-off; human and exoskeleton share one policy, unlike SMAT's separate agents.
papers.feasibility_notes: Reward transfers to MyoAssist, but Hyfydy results may not (see Beyond Kinematics); SAC with 512-512-256 MLPs is light. No code released.

papers.title: Beyond Kinematics: Benchmarking Simulation Fidelity for Muscle-Driven Imitation Learning
papers.code_status: no repository link in arXiv v1 HTML (only hyfydy.com), checked 2026-09-23
papers.api_title: Beyond Kinematics: Benchmarking Simulation Fidelity for Muscle-Driven Imitation Learning
papers.core_idea: Trains the Choi-style Hyfydy pipeline and MuscleMimic (MuJoCo/MyoSim) on the same 140 s Scherpereel clip (subject AB08) and scores activations against EMG. Kinematics are similar; Hyfydy matches EMG better (pooled RMSE, r: 0.164, 0.40 vs 0.344, 0.11).
papers.what_to_take: MyoAssist is MuJoCo-based: expect good kinematics but weak EMG agreement. No policy reached the clip's >2.0 m/s segments; 3D models scored worse than 2D; MuscleMimic with activation penalties failed to step.
papers.left_untested: One subject and walking only; no symmetry or toe-off metrics; no exoskeleton; reward structures differ between pipelines, so simulator and reward effects are confounded.
papers.feasibility_notes: Promises OpenSim-to-MuscleMimic reference data and a subject-specific Hyfydy model; no link in v1 (checked 2026-09-23).

papers.title: Learning Realistic Athletic Sprinting Without Demonstrations
papers.authors_short: Wang, Bianco, Tevet, Hicks, Liu, Delp, Fatahalian
papers.venue: SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 (to appear, per project page); arXiv 2026-09-10
papers.code_status: Bolt simulator and RL envs (github.com/willwng/msk_envs) public, pushed 2026-08; GitHub API detects no licence file (checked 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: Learning Realistic Athletic Sprinting Without Demonstrations
papers.core_idea: Reference-free sprinting: a 136-muscle, 31-DOF sprinter model (from Haralabidis and Hamner models) runs in Bolt, a Warp GPU simulator at about 1000× real time. Reward: forward COM speed minus weighted joint-limit 'pain' torque plus alive bonus; FastTD3 trains in hours.
papers.what_to_take: A reference-free Phase-2 baseline alongside Lambda-Hold: a speed reward suffices when muscles are calibrated. Their MuJoCo-solver variant gave unstable sprint gaits; passive-force calibration removed exploited hip-rotation artefacts.
papers.left_untested: Simulated top speed 12.5 m/s versus 9.65 m/s in the comparison sprinter; no fatigue; no exoskeleton; symmetry deliberately unrewarded; validation against one athlete plus EMG timing.
papers.feasibility_notes: One RTX 6000 PRO used; a 26.2M-sample on-GPU replay buffer may need shrinking for a 32 GB RTX 5090. Bolt repo lacks a licence.

papers.title: A comprehensive, open-source dataset of lower limb biomechanics in multiple conditions of stairs, ramps, and level-ground ambulation and transitions
papers.venue: J Biomech 119:110320; data on Mendeley (10.17632/fcgm3chfff, k9kvm5tn3f, jj3r5f9pnf)
papers.code_status: dataset; MATLAB scripts (STRIDES.m, RUN_OSIM.m) in scripts.zip
papers.api_title: A comprehensive, open-source dataset of lower limb biomechanics in multiple conditions of stairs, ramps, and level-ground ambulation and transitions
papers.core_idea: 22 able-bodied adults; treadmill walking at 28 speeds (0.5 to 1.85 m/s in 0.05 m/s steps, seven trials) plus level ground, ramps and stairs. OpenSim IK and ID at 200 Hz, GRF, 11-muscle EMG, IMUs, goniometers and gait-cycle segmentation as MATLAB tables.
papers.what_to_take: Best-documented 1.25 m/s reference: the exact speed with GRF and OpenSim IK, 22 subjects for subject choice or averaging, and 1.20/1.30 m/s neighbours to test SMAT-style speed scaling against recorded gait.
papers.left_untested: Speeds change within each treadmill trial, so steady 1.25 m/s windows must be cut using the conditions table; no running.
papers.feasibility_notes: CC BY 4.0; 24.5 GB across three Mendeley parts; walking 0.5 to 1.85 m/s.

papers.title: Imitation Learning from Human Motion Alone Does Not Guarantee Biomechanically Plausible Gait Kinetics
papers.code_status: no code link in arXiv v3 HTML (checked 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: Imitation Learning from Human Motion Alone Does Not Guarantee Biomechanically Plausible Gait Kinetics
papers.core_idea: Compares motion-only imitation with kinetics-aware imitation that adds exponential rewards on sagittal GRFs of both feet and centre of pressure, using a torque-driven MuJoCo model and PPO on one participant's treadmill walking at 0.9, 1.2 and 1.5 m/s.
papers.what_to_take: Kinematics matched either way, but motion-only policies showed premature foot contact, prolonged stance and wrong moments. SMAT's reward is motion-only and its toe-off target is stance-dependent: add GRF/CoP terms.
papers.left_untested: Torque-driven, not muscle-driven; one participant; walking only; no exoskeleton; effect on bilateral symmetry not reported.
papers.feasibility_notes: Cheap reward change, but needs a reference with synchronized GRF; MyoAssist's reference npz holds joint coordinates only.

papers.title: Learning Speed-Adaptive Walking Agent Using Imitation Learning with Physics-Informed Simulation
papers.venue: arXiv preprint (under review per arXiv comment)
papers.code_status: no code link in arXiv v1 HTML (checked 2026-09-23)
papers.api_title: Learning Speed-Adaptive Walking Agent Using Imitation Learning with Physics-Informed Simulation
papers.core_idea: Generates speed-varying references by fitting, at 21 gait-phase points, joint angle as a linear function of speed on Camargo treadmill data, applied to LocoMuJoCo's 1.25 m/s clip. VAIL discriminator reward plus exp speed reward (λ=0.5) and a progressive speed curriculum.
papers.what_to_take: One documented answer to SMAT's unspecified speed scaling. A larger speed-reward share produced asymmetric, irregular gait, relevant to weighting SMAT's exp(-5(v−1.25)²) term against imitation terms.
papers.left_untested: Torque-driven skeleton without muscles; walking only, 0.65 to 1.85 m/s; synthetic references matched data only moderately (R² 0.59); no running extrapolation.
papers.feasibility_notes: LocoMuJoCo code MIT, its datasets CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; TRPO, 4000 epochs × 5000 steps; light compute.

papers.title: AMP: Adversarial Motion Priors for Stylized Physics-Based Character Control
papers.code_status: AMP implemented in MimicKit (Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-06-23) and nv-tlabs/ASE (licence not detected by GitHub API)
papers.api_title: AMP: Adversarial Motion Priors for Stylized Physics-Based Character Control
papers.core_idea: Replaces tracking rewards with a least-squares GAN discriminator on state transitions from unstructured clips; style reward max[0, 1−0.25(D−1)²] is combined with a task reward. No phase variable or clip synchronization; a gradient penalty was crucial for stable training.
papers.what_to_take: A Phase-2 option between imitation and reference-free: short sprint clips as a style prior plus a speed task reward, with no phase alignment across speeds.
papers.left_untested: Torque-driven characters only; no biomechanical metrics (GRF, symmetry, toe-off); whether a prior from one sprinter's short clips can shape a muscle-driven sprinter is open.
papers.feasibility_notes: Implemented in MimicKit (Apache-2.0); discriminator adds modest compute but GAN training can be unstable.

papers.title: A biomechanics dataset of healthy human walking at various speeds, step lengths and step widths
papers.api_title: A biomechanics dataset of healthy human walking at various speeds, step lengths and step widths
papers.core_idea: Ten young adults on a split-belt instrumented treadmill: 33 controlled combinations of speed (0.7 to 2.0 m/s), step length and step width. Preferred step length and frequency were defined at a nominal 1.25 m/s. Raw C3D (markers, GRF) plus Visual3D inverse dynamics (MAT).
papers.what_to_take: The one dataset found built around exactly 1.25 m/s, with speed-matched step-length and cadence variations: lets you test how reference cadence alone shifts toe-off and symmetry in imitation.
papers.left_untested: No OpenSim IK in the release (AddBiomechanics has re-processed it); trunk and arms excluded from inverse dynamics; no running.
papers.feasibility_notes: CC0 on figshare; C3D 1.07 GB, MAT 9.05 GB; walking 0.7 to 2.0 m/s.

papers.title: A human lower-limb biomechanics and wearable sensors dataset during cyclic and non-cyclic activities
papers.api_title: A human lower-limb biomechanics and wearable sensors dataset during cyclic and non-cyclic activities
papers.core_idea: Twelve young adults, 11 cyclic and 20 non-cyclic tasks: treadmill walking 0.4 to 1.8 m/s, running 2.0 to 2.5 m/s, inclines, stairs, jumps, cuts. OpenSim (gait2354-based) angles and moments at 200 Hz as CSV, force plates, bilateral EMG and IMUs.

papers.api_title: Three-dimensional data-tracking simulations of sprinting using a direct collocation optimal control approach

papers.title: Muscular strategy shift in human running: dependence of running speed on hip and ankle muscle performance
papers.venue: J Exp Biol 215:1944-1956; data SimTK project runningspeeds
papers.api_title: Muscular strategy shift in human running: dependence of running speed on hip and ankle muscle performance
papers.core_idea: Nine subjects ran overground from slow running to maximal sprinting; above about 7 m/s the strategy shifts from longer strides (ankle plantarflexors) to faster strides (hip muscles). SimTK releases one representative subject (JA1) at 3.56, 5.20, 7.00 and 9.49 m/s with models.
papers.what_to_take: The only open full-body data found near maximal sprint speed (9.49 m/s) across a speed ladder: tests whether a reference-free sprinter reproduces the >7 m/s shift to stride frequency.
papers.left_untested: Archive contents (GRF, strides, markers vs IK) not inspected because the SimTK download timed out; one subject; 2011-era OpenSim formats.
papers.feasibility_notes: MIT Use Agreement (Stanford, 2012); 2 MB zip; overground 3.56 to 9.49 m/s.

cluster_lessons: Every muscle-driven imitation pipeline found uses DeepMimic-style exponential kernels, but widths vary by orders of magnitude with error units: DeepMimic pose 2 / velocity 0.1 (summed, rad), Choi 2026 position 2 / velocity 0.05, KINESIS 200 on keypoint metres / 5 on velocities. SMAT's single exp(-8·err²) for both positions and velocities cannot be interpreted until err's units and summation are fixed (my inference).

Kinematic tracking does not certify physiology: MuscleMimic reports joint-angle r = 0.90 but muscle-EMG r of only 0.2 to 0.6; Beyond Kinematics finds MuJoCo/MyoSim activations far from EMG (pooled r 0.11) versus Hyfydy (0.40); Liu 2026 shows motion-only imitation mis-times foot contact and prolongs stance. SMAT's metabolic and toe-off claims inherit these risks.

Reference symmetry is a design choice: Choi 2026 mirrors its clip across the sagittal plane, and the MyoAssist digest notes segmented.npz builds the left leg by rolling the right 50%. Measure the reference's own left-right r and toe-off before training; UniExo's policy imitating AMASS walking spent only 53% of the cycle in stance, far from SMAT's ~58% toe-off target.

Speed handling is under-documented: none of the papers read uses SMAT's reference-velocity scaling (target speed / reference pelvis speed). Chiu 2024 builds speed-conditioned references from Camargo's 28-speed ladder and finds a larger speed-reward share yields asymmetric gait; Camargo's 1.20/1.25/1.30 m/s trials allow a direct scaled-versus-recorded reference test.

Licences split the field: kinetics-rich lab datasets are CC BY 4.0 or CC0 (Camargo, van der Zee, Scherpereel, Fukuchi 2017/2018, Schreiber 2019, AddBiomechanics), whereas the mocap libraries behind UniExo and LocoMuJoCo (LAFAN1; LocoMuJoCo default datasets, including a single-subject 1.25 m/s walk) are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, and AMASS is installed separately under its own licence. Prefer CC BY/CC0 references for a shareable reconstruction.

Open sprint data are scarce: Haralabidis 2021 (one sprinter, ~10 m/s single-stance clips, CC BY 4.0) and Dorn 2012 (one subject to 9.49 m/s, MIT) are the only near-maximal sets found; other running datasets stop at 4.5 to 5 m/s (Fukuchi 2017, Hamner & Delp 2013) and LAFAN1's two sprint takes are kinematics-only. Reference-free sprinting (Bolt, Lambda-Hold) validated against these sets is the practical Phase-2 route.

Reference processing moves results too: MuscleMimic's Mocap-Body retargeting raised joint-angle and velocity errors versus GMR-Fit; UniExo took knee flexion directly from SMPL because IK produced a crouch; MuscleMimic found early-termination thresholds of 1 m or more converged higher than 0.25 to 0.5 m. Fix the processing pipeline before comparing references.
occupied_claims: Muscle-driven imitation of a public treadmill reference, fine-tuned into hip and ankle exoskeleton assistance across 0.6 to 2.2 m/s and for simulated weakness (Choi et al. 2026, Hyfydy, arXiv 2604.09431).

Multi-skill (walk, turn, backward, run) MuJoCo/MyoLeg imitation from AMASS and LAFAN1 with a co-adaptive hip exoskeleton, tested on six participants at 0.76 to 2.25 m/s (UniExo, arXiv 2609.19690, same group as SMAT).
Head-to-head MuJoCo/MyoSim versus Hyfydy imitation benchmark against EMG on a shared reference (Ahmad et al. 2026, arXiv 2609.21909).
Reference-free, muscle-driven 100 m sprinting on one GPU with comparison to an elite sprinter and EMG timing (Wang et al. 2026, Bolt, arXiv 2609.11083).
Kinetics-aware (GRF/CoP) imitation rewards versus motion-only for walking joint moments (Liu et al. 2026, torque-driven, arXiv 2603.12408).
Speed-conditioned adversarial imitation from synthetic speed-scaled references built on Camargo data (Chiu et al. 2024, torque-driven, arXiv 2412.03949).
Large-scale MuJoCo muscle imitation with walking (1.2 m/s) and running (1.8 m/s) validation against public EMG datasets (MuscleMimic, arXiv 2603.25544; KINESIS, arXiv 2503.14637).

Experiment-free exoskeleton assistance via learning in simulation (Luo et al., Nature 2024, 10.1038/s41586-024-07382-4; title verified here, content covered by the sim_to_real_exo_control and smat_uniexo_line clusters).
open_gaps: No study found isolates how reference choice (dataset, subject, recorded versus speed-scaled, mirrored versus raw) moves left-right symmetry r and toe-off % in muscle-driven imitation; SMAT's Stage-1 targets make this a cheap ablation (MyoAssist npz vs Camargo 1.25 m/s vs van der Zee 1.25 m/s, each raw and mirrored).
No open, full-stride, multi-subject maximal-sprint dataset with GRF was found; Phase-2 validation must rely on single-subject sets (Haralabidis 2021, Dorn 2012) and published summary curves.
Kinetics-aware rewards (GRF/CoP) have not been tested in muscle-driven exoskeleton co-adaptation; whether they correct stance timing (toe-off) in MyoAssist is open.

Provenance of MyoAssist's short_reference_gait.npz (89.8 s, 500 Hz, mean 1.28 m/s) remains undocumented; matching its cadence and joint ranges against Camargo, van der Zee or Scherpereel trials could identify it or justify replacing it.
A hand-over from imitation (walk/jog references) to reference-free speed maximisation (Bolt, Lambda-Hold) within one MuJoCo muscle model with an exoskeleton was not found.

MuJoCo-specific risks at sprint speed are untested in MyoAssist: Beyond Kinematics attributes weaker EMG fidelity partly to inelastic MuJoCo tendons, and the Bolt authors saw unstable sprint gaits with the MuJoCo constraint solver.
unverifiable: The Development of Joint Kinematics, Kinetics and Electromyography Activity over 50 m Sprints in Experienced Sprinters (MDPI, 2026; surfaced by WebSearch): publisher page returned HTTP 403 and Europe PMC had no record, so data availability is unknown; not listed.
Arnold et al. 2013, 'Simulated muscle fiber lengths and velocities during walking and running' (SimTK, per the awesome-biomechanics list): lead only, project page not opened.

Link between AddBiomechanics source 'Carter et al. 2023' (50 subjects, 21.6 h) and the Bath runners dataset (10.15125/BATH-01341; 50 runners, CC BY 4.0, ~28.9 GB, speeds relative to each runner's easy pace; verified via DataCite): plausible but not confirmed.
Contents of Dorn 2012 RunningDataModels.zip (GRF present? full strides?): SimTK download page timed out twice; project page, licence, size and speeds were verified.

Licence of Zenodo 6457662: DataCite lists Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Netherlands, but the WebFetch summary of the record page named no licence and the Zenodo API returned 403; treat as CC BY 3.0 NL pending a direct check.
